description:
I'm interested in NASA's Moon and Mars exploration challenge and want to create an interactive storytelling experience using AI and 3D visualization.

Looking for teammates skilled in web development, 3D modelling, UI/UX design, AI/ML, data visualization, and space science. Creative thinkers and enthusiastic collaborators are welcome!
summary: Martian Map is a turn-by-turn EVA surface navigation system — essentially "Google Maps for Mars" — that layers six NASA datasets (HiRISE imagery, MOLA topography, Viking mosaics, USGS nomenclature, Curiosity 360° panoramas, and REMS meteorology) into a single astronaut-ready interface for hyperlocal Marswalk planning in Gale Crater. It fills the gap between NASA's existing global-scale tools (like Mars Trek) and what the first human explorers will actually need: route-level, slope-aware, obstacle-conscious guidance they can use while wearing spacesuits on an alien surface.
details:
MarScope  

What It Does & How It Works  

Martian Map is a turn-by-turn EVA surface navigation system—essentially a Mars counterpart to familiar mapping tools—built as a spacecraft tablet application for planning and carrying out a Marswalk. It centres on Gale Crater, the zone used by NASA’s Curiosity rover, and combines six real NASA datasets into one tactical interface.  

The application offers four integrated views sharing a single reactive state store:  

  • 3D Terrain HUD (Three.js)  
  • First-person surface view at 1.7 m astronaut eye height, using DEM geometry draped with HiRISE orthophoto imagery  
  • Physically accurate Mars sky model—butterscotch daytime CO₂-scattered atmosphere, blue forward-scattering sunrise/sunset glow, dust haze horizon band driven by optical depth tau, stars at night, and a 0.35° sun disc  
  • Curiosity rover 3D model enabling a third-person camera option  
  • Ground-anchored route lines with chevron indicators, destination beacon poles, and arrival rings  
  • 2D Tactical Mini Map (Leaflet)  
  • High-resolution Gale Crater map from 25 cm/px HiRISE imagery  
  • Switchable among three layer styles: satellite orthophoto, MOLA elevation hillshade, and slope hazard heatmap  
  • Shows astronaut position, heading, and route overlay with heading-up or north-up orientation  
  • Mars Planetary Globe & Flat Map (Three.js)  
  • Interactive 3D globe textured with the Viking MDIM 2.1 colourised global mosaic- Labeled 30° graticule, atmospheric rim glow, and 2,055 USGS/IAU planetary nomenclature features include level-of-detail decluttering.  
  • A pannable flat equirectangular projection offers multiple base layers.  
  • Mars “Street View”  
  • A 360° panoramic viewer uses real Curiosity Mastcam panoramas from multiple sols.  
  • It lets the astronaut preview the surface at waypoints before arrival.  
  • Drag-to-look and pinch-to-zoom follow the Google Street View model.  

Turn-by-Turn Navigation Engine  

  • Great-circle distances and forward azimuths are computed on the IAU 2000 Mars sphere (R = 3,396,190 m) using the Haversine formula.  
  • Human-readable tactical instructions such as “Move forward 40 m” or “Move forward right 285 m” use turn reasoning based on relative bearing from the current heading.  
  • An instruction bar shows remaining distance, estimated walking time at a 1.4 m/s suited astronaut pace, live DEM elevation, and Horn-method ground slope with safety grading below 15°.  
  • A directional waypoint arrow in the 3D HUD points toward the next waypoint; a destination beacon overlay shows the target name and live distance.  
  • Arrival is announced within 5 m of the destination.  

Mars Solar Time & Sun Geometry Simulator  

  • The Allison & McEwen (2000) / Mars24 solar geometry formula is implemented.  
  • Adjusting Local True Solar Time (00:00–24:00 LTST) via slider or quick-jump buttons drives the 3D sun position, surface shadows, sky dome coloring, and lighting in real time.60× playback mode advances one Martian hour every 60 seconds, allowing the astronaut to preview shadow conditions and visibility across a sol before choosing a route.  

Weather & Climate Panel  

  • Modeled on the Google Weather card layout, it presents surface meteorology using Curiosity REMS baseline data.  
  • Current temperature (°C/°F toggle) includes diurnal cycle modeling, peaking at −18°C at 14:00 LTST and dropping to −78°C at 05:00.  
  • Atmospheric pressure shows semi-diurnal thermal tide modeling (~725–770 Pa).  
  • Surface wind speed and direction follow daytime thermal upslope and nighttime downslope cycles.  
  • Dust visibility (optical depth tau) uses an adjustable slider.  
  • Hourly forecast pills and a 5-sol outlook are provided.  
  • Interactive charts track diurnal temperature, pressure, and wind.  
  • Gale Crater rim depth analysis shows current depth below the 5,500 m crater rim.  

Terrain Measurement Tool  

  • Click two points on the map to compute terrain distance, straight-line 3D distance, elevation gain or loss, maximum slope angle with safety assessment, and an elevation profile cross-section. This is vital for route planning in unfamiliar terrain where obstacles may not be visible from a distance.  

Places Catalog & Feature Inspection  

  • A searchable, filterable catalog lists Mars locations, including active rovers (Perseverance, Curiosity), historic missions (Opportunity, Spirit, Pathfinder/Sojourner, Phoenix, InSight, Viking landers), and geographic features.Each entry serves as a detailed “mission dossier” containing coordinates, elevation, scientific instruments, key discoveries, narrative storytelling, and high-resolution imagery carousels. Entries may be set as navigation destinations or viewed on the globe. Filter chips include All Targets, Rover Expeditions, Walkable EVA, and Verified sites.

Benefits  

  • Safety-First Design — Slope hazard heatmaps, live slope grading in the instruction bar (with a 15° EVA safe limit), elevation profile measurement, and weather forecasting provide astronauts with the information needed to avoid terrain hazards and plan around environmental conditions — NASA’s primary priority.  
  • Hyperlocal Scale — Unlike existing tools built for regional or global views, Martian Map operates at the individual Marswalk scale — meter level resolution where route planning decisions occur.  
  • Familiar UX Paradigm — By modeling the interface on Google Maps (turn-by-turn directions, Street View, weather cards, measurement tools), the system uses navigation patterns every astronaut already knows, reducing training time and cognitive load in a high-stress environment.  
  • Multi-Data Fusion — Layers optical, topographic, slope, atmospheric, meteorological, and nomenclature data together in context, so the astronaut sees the full picture rather than consulting separate tools.  
  • Zero-Infrastructure Deployment — Runs entirely client-side with no backend, no API keys, no accounts, and no internet dependency crucial for a Mars habitat where connectivity to Earth has 4–24 minute light-speed delays.  

Intended Impact  

  • Mission Planning — Provide a template for the type of integrated surface navigation system that will be essential when humans reach Mars, showing what is possible with current data and what gaps remain.  
  • Public Engagement — Make Mars exploration tangible and accessible — anyone can open the tool and experience what it would feel like to walk across the Martian surface, building public understanding of and support for human Mars exploration.Data Integration Proof of Concept Demonstrating that combining HiRISE imagery, MOLA topography, REMS meteorology, Mastcam panoramas, and USGS nomenclature into one interface yields value beyond the individual components.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software  

Languages & Frameworks  

  • JavaScript (ES Modules) — all application logic (~7,000 lines of source code)  
  • HTML5 & CSS3 — custom dark aerospace mission-control theme (1,188 lines of CSS), fully responsive layout  

3D & Mapping Libraries  

  • Three.js v0.187 — WebGL terrain rendering, sky simulation, planetary globe, and Street View panoramas  
  • Leaflet v1.9.4 — 2D Mars equirectangular tactical mini-map with custom coordinate reference system  

Build & Test Tooling  

  • Vite v8.3.8 — modern frontend development server and production bundler  
  • Puppeteer Core v25.17 — headless browser regression testing across multiple viewports (1280×800, 1024×768, 768×1024)  

Deployment  

  • GitHub Pages — static hosting, 88 MB total bundle, zero backend services  

Scientific Models & Standards  

  • IAU 2000 Mars Sphere — Haversine great-circle distance, forward azimuth, East-North-Up local tangent plane coordinates  
  • Allison & McEwen (2000) / Mars24 — Mars solar geometry (elevation, azimuth, declination, hour angle)  
  • Horn (1981) Method — 3×3 window slope computation over ≥5 m baseline for terrain safety grading  
  • Lucide (inline SVG) — tactical UI iconography  

NASA Data Sources Used  

  • Mars Viking Colorized Global Mosaic — Viking Orbiters 1 & 2 (MDIM 2.1) — optical imageryMOLA Global Elevation & Hillshade Mars Global Surveyor / Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter topographic data  
  • Gale Crater Color Orthophoto Mosaic — Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter / HiRISE (25 cm/px native) optical imagery  
  • Gale Crater Topographic DEM & Slope — MRO HiRISE Stereo DTM / HRSC Blend topographic data  
  • Planetary Nomenclature Gazetteer — USGS / IAU Working Group (2,055 named features) — geospatial reference  
  • Curiosity Mastcam 360° Panoramas — MSL Curiosity / Mastcam surface optical imagery  
  • Curiosity REMS Surface Meteorology — MSL / Rover Environmental Monitoring Station — atmospheric data  

All data is NASA Public Domain (17 U.S.C. §105), sourced from USGS Astrogeology, NASA PDS, JPL, and the University of Arizona.  

Creativity  

  • "Google Maps for Mars" Paradigm — Rather than constructing another scientific viewer, we reimagined navigation through the most familiar mapping interface on Earth —turn by turn directions, Street View, weather cards, and measurement tools applied to an alien world. This approach makes the tool instantly intuitive for anyone who has used a smartphone.  
  • Mars "Street View" from Real Panoramas — We adapted Curiosity's Mastcam 360° panoramas into an immersive preview system an astronaut can survey their destination before moving there, a capability absent from current Mars tools.Dynamic Mars Sky Simulation — The sky dome is not a fixed backdrop; it is a physically informed model with butterscotch CO₂scattered daylight, blue forward-scattering sunset glow (the reverse of Earth), dust haze that varies with optical depth, and a star field visible at night. Paired with the solar time simulator, you can experience a complete Martian sol.  
  • Minecraft F3-Style Live Coordinates — Drawing from the real-time debug overlay in Minecraft, we included a persistent HUD showing live planetocentric coordinates, MOLA elevation, and compass heading offering the astronaut steady spatial awareness without opening any panel.  
  • Mission Storytelling Dossiers — Each rover and lander is more than a map pin; it carries a detailed narrative with the full mission story, scientific discoveries, instrument payloads, and telemetry data. This shifts navigation into exploration and learning.  
  • Zero-Backend Architecture — The whole system operates with no servers, no API keys, no user accounts, and no internet reliance. Every byte is bundled and served from the same origin, enforced by a strict Content Security Policy. This is not merely a technical choice; it is a design philosophy for a tool that must function 225 million kilometres from the nearest server.  

Factors the Team ConsideredAstronaut Safety as Priority #1 — Each feature was assessed through the question of whether it aids crew movement. Slope hazard maps, elevation profiles, weather forecasting, and real-time terrain grading support this aim.  

  • Spacesuit Mobility Constraints — A 1.4 m/s EVA pace, a 15° slope limit, and step-based controls mirror the physical limits of a pressurized suit carrying scientific gear.  
  • Mars-Specific Environmental Physics — The solar geometry model uses Mars’s 25.19° obliquity; the weather model reflects a thin CO₂ atmosphere (~748 Pa versus Earth’s 101,325 Pa); and the sky model shows blue sunsets from forward-scattering dust.  
  • Data Transparency — Every dataset is marked REAL or SIMULATED in the interface and code registry. Simulated values such as weather curves and micro-terrain detail carry badges, since clear provenance builds trust in a tool astronauts rely on.  
  • Offline-First Design — Because Earth, Mars delays range from 4–24 minutes, the tool avoids real-time links. A static, self-contained design lets it function without any network.  
  • Responsive Design — Tested across viewports (1280×800, 1024×768, 768×1024), it serves as a workstation display, handheld tablet, or portable device during EVA.  
  • WebGL Resource Discipline — Exactly 2 WebGL contexts (terrain HUD plus globe/minimap sharing one renderer) prevent GPU strain on tablet hardware an astronaut might carry.  
  • Accessibility & Discoverability — An 8-step guided tour introduces features; ARIA labels support screen readers; and consistent color language uses cyan for science data, orange for Mars/destination markers, and green for safe status.
